samples.text:
The graph shows the number of new cars which were sold in one country from 2014 to 2024, and it divide them into petrol, diesel, electric and hybrid cars.

In 2014, petrol and diesel cars was the most popular. Petrol had 1,150 thousand sales and diesel had 1,100 thousand. Electric and hybrid cars were very low, only 5 and 30 thousand. After that petrol went up to 1,300 thousand in 2018, but diesel decreased to 700 thousand in the same year.

From 2018 both petrol and diesel fell a lot. In 2020 petrol was 900 thousand and diesel was 280 thousand. In 2024 petrol was 700 thousand and diesel was only 90 thousand, so diesel became the least popular.

In the other hand, electric and hybrid cars increased very fast after 2018. Hybrid cars reached 170 thousand in 2020 and 410 thousand in 2024. Electric cars rose to 270 thousand in 2022 and to 480 thousand in 2024, which was more than hybrid.

Overall, petrol and diesel cars decreased and electric and hybrid cars increased, but petrol was still the highest in 2024.
samples.why: Overview present but placed late · key trends covered mechanically · repetitive vocabulary · agreement errors and an incorrect linking phrase, but meaning is always clear.

samples.text:
The line graph compares annual sales of new cars in one country according to four types of fuel, petrol, diesel, electric and hybrid, from 2014 to 2024.

Overall, there was a clear shift away from conventional fuels towards electric and hybrid vehicles. Although petrol cars remained the best-selling type in 2024, sales of diesel cars collapsed, while those of electric and hybrid cars increased dramatically.

In 2014, petrol and diesel cars dominated the market, with sales of 1,150,000 and 1,100,000 respectively. Petrol sales continued to grow to a peak of 1,300,000 in 2018, whereas diesel sales had already begun to fall, dropping to 700,000 in that year. After 2018, both declined steeply, and by 2024 only 700,000 petrol cars and 90,000 diesel cars were sold.

By contrast, electric and hybrid cars accounted for tiny numbers in 2014, at 5,000 and 30,000. Their sales rose slowly until 2018 and then took off. Hybrid sales reached 320,000 in 2022 and 410,000 in 2024. Electric cars grew even more quickly, and they overtook hybrids in the final two years to reach 480,000, making it the second most popular type.
samples.why: Clear overview of the shift in fuel types · key features and crossovers highlighted · logical grouping · good range of cohesive devices · mostly error-free, with a minor pronoun agreement slip.

samples.text:
The graph illustrates how sales of new cars in one country were divided between petrol, diesel, electric and hybrid models over the decade from 2014 to 2024.

Overall, the market underwent a significant transformation. Diesel sales collapsed and petrol sales, after an initial rise, also contracted, although petrol remained the best-selling fuel type. Meanwhile, electric and hybrid cars rose from near-insignificance to become major players.

In 2014, petrol and diesel cars were almost equally popular, selling 1,150,000 and 1,100,000 units respectively. Their paths soon diverged, however. Petrol sales climbed to a high of 1,300,000 in 2018 before falling to 700,000 by 2024, whereas diesel sales plummeted from 2016 onwards, reaching just 90,000 in 2024, less than a tenth of their original level.

Electric and hybrid vehicles, by contrast, sold only 5,000 and 30,000 units respectively in 2014, and growth remained modest until 2018. From then on, both expanded rapidly. Hybrids reached 320,000 in 2022, overtaking diesel, and continued rising to 410,000. Electric car sales were even more spectacular, surging to 480,000 in 2024 and thereby overtaking hybrids to become the second most popular category.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including crossovers and divergence · clear overview · accurate figures and valid derived comparison · precise, varied vocabulary · wide range of error-free structures.
